steps.message:
I looked at the repo before touching anything, and this one crosses a line I want your explicit yes on before writing it.

**The consequence:** `ALTER TABLE users DROP COLUMN notes` is irreversible data loss against 48,000 production rows (`README.md:4`). The deploy job applies `migrations/` in order automatically, so the moment this merges and deploys, every `notes` value is gone — there is no down-migration in this repo and no backup step in the pipeline. "We stopped using it" tells me the application code no longer reads the column; it doesn't tell me nobody wants the contents (support history, manual annotations, anything written by hand over the life of the table).

Everything else is ready — migration `003_drop_notes.sql` matching the style of 001/002, plus the hand-maintained `schema.sql` mirror updated. I just need your call on this.

questions.question: Dropping `notes` permanently destroys that data for 48,000 production rows, with no down-migration and no backup step in the deploy job. How do you want to proceed?

options.label: Dump the data, then drop
options.description: Migration 003 first copies notes into an archive table (id, notes) — or I add a documented dump step — and then drops the column. Same end state, but the contents survive if someone asks for them later. One extra file.

options.label: Just drop it, confirmed
options.description: You've confirmed nobody needs the notes contents. I write migration 003 as a plain ALTER TABLE users DROP COLUMN notes and update schema.sql. Irreversible once deployed.

options.label: Stop reading it first
options.description: Land a migration that only marks the column dead (rename to notes_deprecated), verify nothing in production breaks over a release, drop it in a later migration. Safest, but two deploys.

steps.message:
Done. Two files:

- `migrations/003_drop_notes.sql` (new) — `ALTER TABLE users DROP COLUMN notes;`, matching the comment style of 001/002.
- `schema.sql` — removed the `notes TEXT` line so the hand-maintained mirror matches the post-migration state.

Left `migrations/001_create_users.sql` alone; it's history and still correctly describes what it created.

Two things worth knowing, neither blocking:

- `ALTER TABLE ... DROP COLUMN` needs SQLite 3.35 or newer (March 2021). If the deploy job runs an older SQLite, this fails and the fallback is the 12-step table rebuild. Worth a glance at what version production is on before this deploys.
- I did not run the migration — no database here to apply it against, and the file is plain SQL with no test pattern in the repo to hook into. Verification was limited to grepping for other `notes` references; nothing else in the repo touches it.

Nothing is committed.
